groups.name: Basics
groups.description: Five short examples, in order. Start here if you have not used a microcontroller before.

groups.name: Sensors
groups.description: Reading the world: temperature, distance, movement, light and magnetic fields.

groups.name: Displays and LEDs
groups.description: Showing something, from a character display to a matrix or a strip of colour.

groups.name: Motion
groups.description: Making something move, with motors and servos.

groups.name: Input
groups.description: Taking something in from a person: knobs, keypads and card readers.

groups.name: Remote control
groups.description: Talking over infrared, in both directions.

groups.name: Between boards
groups.description: Getting two boards to talk to each other, by radio or down a wire.

groups.name: Networking
groups.description: Wifi, access points, name lookups and MQTT. Needs a board with a radio: an ESP32 or a Pico W.

groups.name: Bluetooth
groups.description: Finding devices, being one, and connecting to one over Bluetooth Low Energy.

groups.name: Storage and time
groups.description: Remembering things after the power goes, and knowing what time it is.

groups.name: Tools
groups.description: Finding out what is really on the bus.

examples.title: 1. Blink an LED — digital write
examples.description: The first program on any microcontroller. Turns a pin on and off to blink an LED, which is all a digital write is.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 2. Button — digital read
examples.description: When the button is pressed the onboard led (at least for the ESP32) will turn on. It will turn of when the button is released. Shows what a digital read is, and why a pull-up resistor is needed to read a switch.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 3. Analog Read — measuring a knob
examples.description: Measures a voltage with the analog to digital converter and prints it as a raw number, as volts and as a percentage. Turn a potentiometer and watch it change.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 4. PWM — analog write
examples.description: This example will show you how to create a fading LED animation with a PWM Signal.  This example can of course also be used to control servo's, motor drivers, buzzers, analog output, etc. Shows what an analog write is: switching a pin fast enough that a fraction of the time on behaves like a voltage in between.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 5. Dimmer — putting them together
examples.description: Reads a potentiometer and dims an LED to match, showing how to map any input range onto any output range.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: DHT Sensor Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller should display the temperature and humidity in the console. This information is collected from a DHT11 or DHT22 sensor.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C BMP280 Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads the temperature and pressure from the connected BMP280 sensor and prints it on the terminal.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C Compass (GY-271) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads the magnetic field from a GY-271 or HW-246 compass module and prints the three axes and a heading in degrees.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C MPU-6050
examples.description: In this example the microcontrollers reads values from the MPU-6050 accelerometer and gyroscope. It also reads the onboard temperature sensor of the module.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: VCNL4040 Sensor Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads proximity and ambient light from a VCNL4040 sensor, printing the light level in lux and reporting when something comes near.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: TOF10120 Sensor Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller should display the distance that the sensor has measured. This value has a maximum of 2000.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: VL6180X Sensor Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller measures the distance to a nearby object with a VL6180X time of flight sensor, checks whether the reading is valid, and also prints the ambient light level.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Ultrasonic Distance Sensor (HC-SR04)
examples.description: The HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor uses sonar to determine the distance to an object.  This sensor reads from 2cm to 400cm with an accuracy of 0.3cm. In this example, the microcontroller reads the distance from the sensor and displays it on the
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C Liquid Crystal Display Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller should display some text on a Liquid Crystal Display (16x2) over I2C. Keep in mind that the LCD needs an I2C Backpack for this example to work.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: P9813 RGB LED Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller shows the plain colours on a chain of P9813 RGB LEDs and then cycles a rainbow along it.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Seven Segment Display (74HC595) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller drives a single 7-segment display through a 74HC595 shift register, counting 0 to 9 and then through the hex letters, using three pins instead of eight.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: SPI LED Matrix (MAX7219) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller shows text on a chain of MAX7219 8x8 LED matrix modules and scrolls a message across them.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: SPI ST7789 Display Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller should display some text on a ST7789 240x240 Display over SPI.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: TM1637 7-Segment Display Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller writes numbers and text to a TM1637 four digit 7-segment display, then counts minutes and seconds with a blinking colon.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: DC Motor (L293D / L298N) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller drives a DC motor through an H bridge, ramping the speed up, coasting, running backwards and braking.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Servo
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller drives a hobby servo: a positional one to an angle and back, or a 360 degree one at a speed in both directions.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Stepper Motor
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller turns a stepper motor a quarter turn at a time, back to where it started, and then releases it. Works with a 28BYJ-48 on a ULN2003 board or a motor on a step and direction driver.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Matrix Keypad (4x4) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads a membrane matrix keypad, collects the digits typed into a code, and checks it when the hash key is pressed.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: Rotary Encoder
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads a rotary encoder, counting up and down within a range as the knob is turned, and resetting when it is pressed.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: SPI RFID RC522 Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads the id of any MIFARE card or tag held against an RFID-RC522 reader, and prints the contents of one block from it.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: IR Remote (NEC) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller decodes button presses from an infrared remote control with a 38kHz receiver module, prints which button was pressed and toggles the onboard LED.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: IR Remote Send (NEC) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller sends NEC remote control codes from an infrared LED, using the ESP32's RMT peripheral where it exists and a PWM carrier everywhere else.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: nRF24 Radio: Sending
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller sends a counter over a 2.4GHz radio link once a second, and reports whether each packet was acknowledged by the other board.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: nRF24 Radio: Receiving
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller listens for packets over a 2.4GHz radio link, prints the counter in each one and reports any that went missing.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: RS-485 Link (MAX485)
examples.description: In this example two boards talk to each other over RS-485: one asks a question every second and the other answers, over a pair of wires that works across a building.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 1. Joining a Wifi Network
examples.description: Connects to a wifi network using the network module directly, showing the status codes as it goes and printing the address, gateway and DNS server it was given.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 2. Scanning for Networks
examples.description: Lists the wifi networks in range with their channel, signal strength and whether they are open, strongest first.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 3. Running an Access Point
examples.description: Turns the board into a wifi network of its own and serves a small web page to any phone or laptop that joins it, which is how a device with no screen gets set up.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 4. DNS and Fetching a Page
examples.description: Looks up several hostnames to see which DNS server the router handed out and how long each lookup takes, then fetches a page over a plain socket.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 5. MQTT
examples.description: Publishes readings to an MQTT broker and listens for commands coming back, which is how most small devices send their data somewhere useful.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 1. Scanning for BLE Devices
examples.description: Lists the Bluetooth Low Energy devices advertising nearby, with their signal strength, whether they can be connected to and which services they offer.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 2. A BLE Peripheral
examples.description: Turns the board into a Bluetooth device that advertises a temperature service, which a phone or another board can connect to, read from and subscribe to.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: 3. A BLE Central
examples.description: Finds the peripheral from the previous example, connects to it, reads its temperature and then subscribes so new readings arrive on their own.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C EEPROM Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller stores a boot counter and a message in an I2C EEPROM, so they survive the power being cut, and reads them back.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C RTC (DS3231) Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontroller reads the date, time and temperature from a DS3231 real time clock module, and copies the time into the board's own clock so it survives a reset.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

examples.title: I2C Scanner Example
examples.description: In this example the microcontrollers scans for devices connected over I2C and displays them to the user on the console.
examples.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Bluetooth LE (aioble)
drivers.description: The aioble library: Bluetooth Low Energy with asyncio, for scanning, advertising and connecting. Included in Pico W firmware already, and needed on an ESP32.
drivers.author: Jim Mussared

drivers.name: BMP280
drivers.description: Temperature and pressure driver for the Bosch BMP280 over I2C or SPI.
drivers.author: David Stenwall

drivers.name: DHT11 and DHT22 readings
drivers.description: Temperature and humidity from DHT11 and DHT22 sensors, adding retries, the minimum interval between readings, Fahrenheit and dew point on top of the firmware's dht module.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: DS3231 real time clock
drivers.description: Reads and sets the DS3231 real time clock over I2C, including its temperature, and copies the time into the board's own clock.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: I2C EEPROM (24LC, AT24C, CAT24C)
drivers.description: Reads and writes the 24-series I2C EEPROMs, handling page boundaries and write cycles so stored data survives a power cut intact.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: GY-271 compass (QMC5883L / HMC5883L)
drivers.description: Three axis magnetometer driver for the GY-271 and HW-246 compass modules, detecting whether the board carries a QMC5883L or an HMC5883L.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: HC-SR04
drivers.description: Ultrasonic distance driver for the HC-SR04, reading 2cm to 400cm.
drivers.author: Roberto Sánchez

drivers.name: I2C character LCD
drivers.description: HD44780 character LCD driver for displays behind a PCF8574 I2C backpack.
drivers.author: Dave Hylands

drivers.name: IR receiver (NEC remotes)
drivers.description: Decodes NEC infrared remote controls with a three pin 38kHz receiver module such as the CHQ1838, VS1838B or TSOP1838.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: IR transmitter (NEC remotes)
drivers.description: Sends NEC infrared remote codes from an IR LED, using the ESP32's RMT peripheral where it exists and a PWM carrier everywhere else.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Matrix keypad
drivers.description: Reads the membrane matrix keypads, 4x4 and 4x3, with debouncing and one report per key press.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: MAX7219 LED matrix
drivers.description: Driver for chained MAX7219 8x8 LED matrix modules over SPI, with framebuf drawing and text.
drivers.author: Mike Causer

drivers.name: MFRC522 RFID (RC522)
drivers.description: Reads and writes MIFARE Classic cards and tags with an RFID-RC522 reader over SPI.
drivers.author: Stefan Wendler

drivers.name: DC motor on an H bridge (L293D, L298N)
drivers.description: Speed and direction for DC motors on an H bridge driver such as the L293D, the L298N module, the DRV8833 or the TB6612.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: MPU-6050
drivers.description: Accelerometer, gyroscope and temperature driver for the MPU-6050 over I2C.

drivers.name: nRF24L01+ radio
drivers.description: Two way 2.4GHz radio link between boards with nRF24L01+ modules, with addressing, automatic acknowledgement and retries.
drivers.author: micropython-lib contributors

drivers.name: P9813 RGB LED driver
drivers.description: Drives chains of P9813 constant current RGB LEDs, as used by chainable RGB LED modules and clocked RGB strips, over a clock and a data pin.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Addressable LEDs (WS2812B / SK6812)
drivers.description: Brightness, gamma and HSV colour layer for WS2812B, WS2811 and SK6812 RGBW strips, on top of the built-in neopixel module.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Rotary encoder (KY-040)
drivers.description: Reads a rotary encoder with CLK, DT and SW pins from interrupts, counting detents with an optional range, wrapping and a debounced push switch.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: RS-485 (MAX485)
drivers.description: Half duplex RS-485 through a MAX485 or similar transceiver, holding the direction line until the last bit has actually left the wire.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Hobby servo
drivers.description: Drives the three wire hobby servos by pulse length: an angle for a positional servo, a speed for a continuous rotation one.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: 74HC595 shift register
drivers.description: Drives one or more chained 74HC595 shift registers from three pins, turning them into eight outputs each.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: SSD1306 OLED
drivers.description: Monochrome SSD1306 OLED driver for I2C and SPI, with framebuf drawing primitives.
drivers.author: micropython-lib contributors

drivers.name: ST7789 display
drivers.description: Pure MicroPython driver for ST7789 SPI colour displays, with an 8x16 VGA font.
drivers.author: Russ Hughes

drivers.name: Stepper motor (ULN2003, A4988)
drivers.description: Turns stepper motors a known number of steps: four coil pins through a ULN2003 or an H bridge, or two pins to a step and direction driver such as an A4988.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: TC74 temperature
drivers.description: Reads whole degrees Celsius from a Microchip TC74 digital temperature sensor over I2C.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: TM1637 7-segment display
drivers.description: Driver for TM1637 four digit 7-segment LED display modules, over the chip's own two wire protocol.
drivers.author: Mike Causer

drivers.name: MQTT client (umqtt.simple)
drivers.description: The umqtt.simple MQTT client, for boards whose firmware does not already include it, such as the Raspberry Pi Pico W.
drivers.author: micropython-lib contributors

drivers.name: VCNL4040 proximity and light
drivers.description: Proximity and ambient light driver for the Vishay VCNL4040, reading lux and a near field proximity count over I2C.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: VL6180X range and light
drivers.description: Time of flight distance and ambient light driver for the ST VL6180X, measuring millimetres up to about 20cm.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa

drivers.name: Wifi and access points
drivers.description: Joining a wifi network or running an access point, the same way on an ESP32 and a Raspberry Pi Pico W, with the status codes and setup order each port really needs.
drivers.author: Steven Slaa
